{{Short description|Australian astronomer}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2019}}
[[File:Peter Quinn, May 2011.jpg|thumb|Peter Quinn in 2011]]
'''Professor Peter Quinn''' is Executive Director of the [[International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research]] (ICRAR) in [[Perth]], Western Australia<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.icrar.org/contact/staff_pages?image=1764306 |title=Staff: International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research |website=www.icrar.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111016232615/http://www.icrar.org/contact/staff_pages?image=1764306 |archive-date=2011-10-16}}</ref> and was previously the Head of the Data Management and Operations Division at the [[European Southern Observatory]] (ESO) in [[Munich]].<ref name="UWAProfile">{{Cite web|url= http://www.uwa.edu.au/people/peter.quinn |title= Professor Peter Quinn Staff Profile |publisher= The University of Western Australia |access-date= 1 November 2015}}</ref>

Prof. Quinn has authored more than 300 published scientific papers<ref name="UWAProfile" /> and was awarded the 'Western Australian Scientist of the Year' in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://archive.industry.gov.au/ministerarchive2013/chrisevans/mediareleases/pages/topskaastronomernamedwascientistoftheyear.aspx.htm |title=Top SKA astronomer named WA Scientist of the Year |access-date=22 October 2014 |archive-date=5 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150405105852/http://archive.industry.gov.au/ministerarchive2013/chrisevans/mediareleases/pages/topskaastronomernamedwascientistoftheyear.aspx.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Prof. Quinn is also a Fellow of [[Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.icrar.org/news/news_items/media-releases/top-uwa-astronomer-honoured-by-election-to-technology-academy |title=Top UWA astronomer honoured by election to technology academy: International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research |website=www.icrar.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141022195015/http://www.icrar.org/news/news_items/media-releases/top-uwa-astronomer-honoured-by-election-to-technology-academy |archive-date=2014-10-22}}</ref>

At ESO, Prof. Quinn was working towards the creation of the [http://www.euro-vo.org/ Astrophysical Virtual Observatory], a massive virtual [[database]] of astronomical data, designed to allow [[astrophysicist]]s to carry out research using existing data without using valuable [[telescope]] time.

Prior to working at ESO, Prof. Quinn taught astrophysics at the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech) for several years, working alongside [[Gerald Jay Sussman]], and has worked at the NASA [[Space Telescope Science Institute]] (STScI) in [[Baltimore]]. His scientific interests include the study of [[dark matter]], computational [[physical cosmology|cosmology]], [[galactic formation]], and [[MACHOs]].
